cves.summary: Flowise before 3.1.0 (affected versions 3.0.13 and earlier) uses weak hardcoded default JWT secrets ('auth_token', 'refresh_token') and default audience and issuer values ('AUDIENCE', 'ISSUER') in the enterprise passport
cves.headline: Flowise before 3.1.0 lets attackers forge admin JWTs and bypass login

name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
title: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in LLM application platforms, as the single CVE here shows. CVE-2026-56271 affects Flowise, a tool for building LLM apps and agents, before version 3.1.0. The product ships with a fixed cryptographic key baked into its code, so the same secret exists in every copy. Because that key signs login tokens, anyone who learns it can mint their own admin token and walk past the login screen. The result is full administrative access to the platform, including the flows, credentials and connected models it manages. One hard-coded value in a widely deployed AI builder undermines the whole authentication layer.
description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

mitigations.description: Prevention schemes mirror that of hard-coded password storage.

consequences.note: If hard-coded cryptographic keys are used, it is almost certain that malicious users will gain access through the account in question. The use of a hard-coded cryptographic key significantly increases the possibility that encrypted data may be recovered.
